speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Hold still, Arthur. The hem is the work, and the work is done when it is in the hand, not when a book says it is owed.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: Edith let the hem down two fingers at Easter, sir, and my shins are out in the wind again. Make the next lady tall and angry about it!

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will make her tall when I have a lady to make. This morning I have an old man, and he does not care about thy shins.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Payment on delivery. The weather is your trouble, Master Shakespeare, not my thread's.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not offering you the weather. I am not offering you a sum either. John pays what John has agreed. I do not keep the stock in my sleeve.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: Then the stock may keep its sleeve, and I will keep my knees out of the wind if the thread holds. It held at Easter. It has given up.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: It has not given up. You have grown. I let it down. I am not a miracle, and I am not a creditor. If there is more work, it is paid when I put it in the hand.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There is no more work from me this morning. The coat for two of the clock is the old one. I came to see that the boy can walk in it.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: I can walk. I can also hear you from the passage if you shout the tale, which you will, because you love a tale that will not hurry.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not hurry him. The sense is the length. If I help him go faster I lose the only thing he has.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Then shout it in the yard, and not over my thread. I have a cuff to finish and a boy who will not stand on two feet.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: Two feet, Mistress. I am only tall. The fault is the fashion, which was cut for a shorter lad and a kinder month.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The month is hot, and the fashion is what we have. Thou wilt do. I am not writing thee a new gown before dinner.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Good. A new gown is a new bill, and a new bill is coin. I have said my terms. I am not saying them twice for a poet's memory.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have them. Delivery, and coin, and not a promise. I am not opening June again to improve it.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: June was when the cloak went and the sleeves stayed. I was in the doorway, being tall. I am still in a doorway. The doorway has not grown. I have.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: And you may stay in it while I finish. Master Shakespeare, your old man is not in this basket. Go and find him.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He is on the roll. I am going to him. Arthur, stand where she tells thee. The wind is not my office.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: The wind is nobody's office, sir, and it has found my shins without a warrant.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Done. The cuff will hold the afternoon. If it does not, you will tell Master Phillips, and he will tell me, and I will be paid for the mending when it is done. Not before.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not before. Thank you, Mistress. I have a tale to keep long, and a dinner between.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: And I have a skirt that is honest for another week, if I do not breathe. Wish me a small part.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I wish thee the part that is written. I am the old man this afternoon, and he is not small.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Then take him away. My basket is a basket again.

speaker: arthur_meeks
text: Away he goes. Mind the step, sir. The coat is longer than your patience, and so am I.
